comments.author: Slunk_
comments.body_html:
Hey RuKira just to make sure I asked chat GPT the same question you did and heres what it told me

Commenter’s Concern in Plain English:

The commenter is saying:

  • “The Realism Mod hasn’t been officially released for 3.11 on the SPT Hub.”
  • Therefore, your mod, which depends on it, shouldn’t technically be published yet either.
  • They’re drawing a line between “testing releases” (on GitHub) and “official releases” (on the SPT Hub).
  • They question whether it’s allowed to have mods that depend on these “unofficial” testing versions.

The Key Question: Are You Doing Anything Wrong?

✅ What You’re Allowed to Do:

  • Yes, it is allowed to release a mod that depends on a test version of another mod, especially if:

    • You clearly state which version is needed.
    • You’re not bundling any proprietary or closed-source files
    • You’re pointing users to a publicly available GitHub release of the required mod.

  • The Realism test release on GitHub is public, so you’re not breaking any licensing or distribution rules by depending on it.

  • Many modders release things that depend on WIP/test versions—this is common in modding communities.

❌ What Would Be Wrong (But You’re Not Doing):

  • Bundling all Realism’s code/configs
  • Claiming your mod works with the official Hub version when it doesn’t.
  • Misleading users about compatibility.

⚠️ Clarifications You Should Consider Adding (If Not Already):

To reduce confusion and avoid more comments like that one, make sure your mod description clearly states:

  • It requires the 3.11 testing version of Realism (with link to GitHub).
  • The Realism mod is in active development for 3.11 and not yet on the SPT Hub.
  • Your mod is designed specifically around that version.
  • Optional: Note that compatibility might break when Realism officially updates.

Example disclaimer to add:

⚠️ This mod requires the 3.11 Testing Release of the Realism Mod. You can find it here: [GitHub Link].

The Realism Mod has not yet been officially published on the SPT Hub for 3.11, so please use at your own discretion. This mod may require updates when Realism is finalized.

✅ Conclusion:

You are not doing anything wrong, technically or ethically.

You’re using a public test release, not violating terms, and not bundling unauthorized files. As long as you’re transparent in your documentation and provide clear instructions, you’re fine.

The commenter seems to misunderstand the distinction between what’s “published on the hub” and what’s “available for use.” There’s no rule saying your mod can’t exist just because it depends on a test version.

Let me know if you want help drafting a response to them or adding clarifying language to your mod page.

for example the original game had 4 desert eagles in .50AE. this fix will hopefully come in later updates once I figure it out. (need to teach myself to modify this first) but for now its meant to be for hardcore rule set where you aren’t even supposed to buy anything. or just know this quirk I guess. it is what it is.
